title.zh: 卷八十六 列傳第二十四: 李石子:獻可 完顏福壽 獨吉義 烏延蒲離黑 烏延蒲轄奴 烏延查剌 李師雄 尼厖古鈔兀 孛朮魯定方 夾谷胡剌 蒲察斡論 夾谷查剌
title.en: Volume 86 Biographies 24: Li Shi son: Xianke, Wanyan Fushou, Du Jiyi, Wuyanpulihei, Wuyanpuxianu, Wuyanchala, Li Shixiong, Nipangguchaowu, Beipailudingfang, Jia Guhula, Pu Chawolun, Jia Guchala
title.raw: 卷八十六 列傳第二十四: 李石子:獻可 完顏福壽 獨吉義 烏延蒲離黑 烏延蒲轄奴 烏延查剌 李師雄 尼厖古鈔兀 孛朮魯定方 夾谷胡剌 蒲察斡論 夾谷查剌 Volume 86 Biographies 24: Li Shi son: Xianke, Wanyan Fushou, Du Jiyi, Wuyanpulihei, Wuyanpuxianu, Wuyanchala, Li Shixiong, Nipangguchaowu, Beipailudingfang, Jia Guhula, Pu Chawolun, Jia Guchala

sentences.zh: 李石，字子堅，遼陽人，貞懿皇后弟也。

translations.literal: Li Shi, style name Zijian, was a man of Liaoyang and younger brother of Empress Zhenyì.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, whose courtesy name was Zijian, came from Liaoyang and was the younger brother of Empress Zhenyì.

sentences.zh: 先世仕遼，為宰相。

translations.literal: His forebears had served the Liao and been chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had served the Liao dynasty as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 高祖仙壽，嘗脫遼主之舅于難，遼帝賜仙壽遼陽及湯池地千頃，他物稱是，常以李舅目之。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xianshou once rescued the Liao ruler's maternal uncle from peril; the Liao emperor granted Xianshou a thousand qing of land in Liaoyang and Tangchi, with other goods in proportion, and customarily called him Uncle Li.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xianshou had once saved the Liao emperor's maternal uncle from danger; the Liao emperor rewarded him with a thousand qing of land in Liaoyang and Tangchi, along with commensurate gifts, and habitually referred to him as Uncle Li.

sentences.zh: 父雛訛只，桂州觀察使，高永昌據東京，率眾攻之，不勝而死。

translations.literal: His father Chun'e-zhi was military commissioner of Gui Prefecture; when Gao Yongchang seized Dongjing, he led troops to attack him, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chun'e-zhi served as military commissioner of Gui Prefecture; when Gao Yongchang seized Dongjing, he led an army against him, was defeated, and died in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 石敦厚寡言，而器識過人。

translations.literal: Shi was deep and sparing of speech, yet his capacity and insight surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was reserved and sparing of words, yet his judgment and insight surpassed those of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，授世襲謀克，為行軍猛安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui he was granted a hereditary mouke and made campaigning meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhui he received a hereditary mouke and was appointed campaigning meng'an.

sentences.zh: 睿宗為右副元帥，引置軍中，屬之宗弼。

translations.literal: When Prince Ruizong was deputy right commander-in-chief, he brought Shi into the army and assigned him to Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ruizong served as deputy right commander-in-chief, he brought Shi into his forces and placed him under Zongbi's command.

sentences.zh: 八年，除禮賓副使，轉洛苑副使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made deputy commissioner of protocol guest affairs, then transferred to deputy commissioner of the Luo Park.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed deputy commissioner of protocol guest affairs, then transferred to deputy commissioner of the Luo Park.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，置行台省于汴，石為汴京都巡檢使，曆大名少尹、汴京馬軍副都指揮使，累官景州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan, when the Branch Secretariat was established at Bian, Shi became metropolitan patrol inspector of Bianjing; he successively held vice magistrate of Daming, deputy commander-in-chief of the Bianjing horse army, and rose to inspector of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjuan, when the Branch Secretariat was set up at Bian, Shi became metropolitan patrol inspector of Bianjing; he went on to serve as vice magistrate of Daming and deputy commander-in-chief of the Bianjing horse army, and eventually rose to inspector of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 海陵營建燕京宮室，石護役皇城端門。

translations.literal: When Hailing built the palaces at Yanjing, Shi supervised labor on the Duan Gate of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hailing undertook construction of the palaces at Yanjing, Shi oversaw work on the Duan Gate of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 海陵遷都燕京，石隨例入見。

translations.literal: When Hailing moved the capital to Yanjing, Shi followed precedent to attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing moved the capital to Yanjing, Shi presented himself for audience as custom required.

sentences.zh: 海陵指石曰：「此非葛王之舅乎？」

translations.literal: Hailing pointed at Shi and said, Is this not Prince Ge's maternal uncle?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing pointed at Shi and said, "Is this not Prince Ge's maternal uncle?"

sentences.zh: 葛王，謂世宗也。

translations.literal: Prince Ge meant Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ge referred to Shizong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除興中少尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed vice magistrate of Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed vice magistrate of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 石知海陵忌宗室，頗歉前日之言，秩滿，托疾還鄉里。

translations.literal: Shi knew Hailing was jealous of the imperial clan and regretted his words of the other day; when his term expired he pleaded illness and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Shi knew that Hailing was suspicious of the imperial clan and regretted what he had said; when his term ended, he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 世宗留守東京，禦契丹括裏，石留東京巡察城中。

translations.literal: When Shizong was left to garrison Dongjing and repelled the Khitan Kuoli, Shi remained in Dongjing to patrol the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was left behind to garrison Dongjing and repelled the Khitan Kuoli, Shi stayed in the city to patrol its defenses.

sentences.zh: 海陵使副留守高存福伺察世宗動靜，知軍李蒲速越知存福謀，以告世宗，石因勸世宗先除存福，然後舉事，世宗從之。

translations.literal: Hailing sent Deputy Left Behind Gao Cunfu to watch Shizong's movements; army supervisor Li Pusuyue learned of Cunfu's plot and reported to Shizong; Shi urged Shizong to eliminate Cunfu first and then act, and Shizong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had sent Deputy Left Behind Gao Cunfu to spy on Shizong; the army supervisor Li Pusuyue discovered Cunfu's plot and informed Shizong, whereupon Shi urged him to remove Cunfu first and only then raise his standard. Shizong followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 大定元年，以定策功為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading, for his merit in settling the succession he was made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dading he was appointed Minister of Revenue for his role in securing the succession.

sentences.zh: 無何，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 阿瑣殺同知中都留守蒲察沙離只，遣使奉表東京，而群臣多勸世宗幸上京者。

translations.literal: A Suo killed the associate left-behind of the Central Capital, Pucha Salizhi, and sent envoys with a memorial to Dongjing; meanwhile many among the ministers urged Shizong to go to the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: A Suo killed the associate left-behind of the Central Capital, Pucha Salizhi, and sent envoys bearing a memorial to Dongjing, while many ministers urged Shizong to proceed to the Upper Capital instead.

sentences.zh: 石奏曰：「正隆遠在江、淮，寇盜蜂起，萬姓引領東向，宜因此時直赴中都，據腹心以號令天下，萬世之業也。

translations.literal: Shi memorialized: Zhenglong is far away on the Jiang and Huai; bandits are rising everywhere; the people are all looking east. Your Majesty should seize this moment and go straight to the Central Capital, hold the heartland and command the realm—this is an enterprise for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Shi memorialized: "The Zhenglong emperor is far away on the Jiang and Huai; bandits are rising on every side; the people are straining eastward. Your Majesty should seize this moment and march straight for the Central Capital, hold the heartland, and command the realm—this is an enterprise for the ages.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下無牽于眾惑。」

translations.literal: Only let Your Majesty not be drawn by the multitude's confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Only do not let Your Majesty be swayed by the crowd's confusion."

sentences.zh: 上意遂決，即日啟行。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was decided; he set out the same day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up, and he set out that very day.

sentences.zh: 世宗納石女後宮，生鄭王永蹈、衛紹王永濟，是為元妃李氏。

translations.literal: Shizong took Shi's daughter into the inner palace; she bore Prince Yong of Zheng Yongtao and Prince Yong of Wei Yongji—this was Consort Yuan, Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong took Shi's daughter into the inner palace; she bore Prince Yong of Zheng, Yongtao, and Prince Yong of Wei, Yongji—she was Consort Yuan, Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 三年，戶部尚書梁钅求上言：「大定以前，官吏士卒俸粟支帖真偽相雜，請一切停罷。」

translations.literal: In the third year, Minister of Revenue Liang Qiu memorialized: Before Dading, the grain salary warrant notes issued to officials, clerks, and soldiers were mixed with forgeries; I request that they all be discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Minister of Revenue Liang Qiu memorialized: "Before Dading, the grain salary warrant notes issued to officials, clerks, and soldiers were rife with forgeries; I ask that they all be abolished."

sentences.zh: 石買革去舊貼，下倉支粟，倉司不敢違，以新粟與之。

translations.literal: Shi bought up and destroyed the old warrants, ordered the granaries to issue grain, and the granary officials dared not disobey, giving them new grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shi bought up and destroyed the old warrants, ordered the granaries to issue grain, and the granary officials dared not refuse, supplying them with new grain instead.

sentences.zh: 上聞其事，以問梁钅求。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the matter, he questioned Liang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he questioned Liang Qiu about it.

sentences.zh: 梁钅求對不以實。

translations.literal: Liang Qiu did not answer truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qiu did not answer truthfully.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書左丞翟永固鞫之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Left Vice Grand Councillor Zhai Yonggu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Left Vice Grand Councillor Zhai Yonggu to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 梁钅求削官四階，降知火山軍，石罷為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Liang Qiu was reduced four ranks in office and demoted to know the Huoshan Army; Shi was dismissed and made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qiu was stripped of four ranks and demoted to administrator of the Huoshan Army; Shi was removed from office and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 久之，封道國公。

translations.literal: After some time he was enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo.

sentences.zh: 六年，上幸西京，石與少詹事烏古論三合守衛中都宮闕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited Xijing, Shi and Junior Household Steward Wugulun Sanhe guarded the palaces and passes of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited Xijing, Shi and Junior Household Steward Wugulun Sanhe were left to guard the palaces and passes of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「京師巡禦，不可不嚴。

translations.literal: An edict said: Patrol and defense of the capital cannot but be strict.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Patrol and defense of the capital must be strict.

sentences.zh: 近都猛安內選士二千人巡警，仍給口豢芻粟。」

translations.literal: Two thousand men were selected from meng'an near the capital to patrol, and they were still given grain for persons and draft animals.
translations.idiomatic: Select two thousand men from the meng'an near the capital for patrol duty, and continue to supply grain for persons and draft animals."

sentences.zh: 謂宰臣曰：「府庫錢幣非徒聚貨也，若軍士貧弱，百姓困乏，所費雖多，豈可已哉？」

translations.literal: He told the chief ministers: Treasury coin is not merely hoarded goods; if soldiers are poor and weak or the people are distressed and exhausted, however much is spent, how can it be stopped?
translations.idiomatic: He told the chief ministers: "Treasury funds are not mere hoarded wealth; if soldiers are impoverished or the people are in distress, no matter how much is spent, how can it be withheld?"

sentences.zh: 故事，凡行幸，留守中都官每十日表問起居。

translations.literal: By precedent, whenever the emperor traveled, the officials left behind at the Central Capital every ten days submitted a memorial inquiring after his health.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, whenever the emperor traveled, the officials left behind at the Central Capital submitted a memorial inquiring after his health every ten days.

sentences.zh: 上以使傳頻煩，命二十日一進表。

translations.literal: Because dispatch bearers were too frequent, the emperor ordered memorials submitted once every twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the courier traffic too burdensome, the emperor ordered that memorials be submitted only once every twenty days.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜司徒，兼太子太師，御史大夫如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, while remaining Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, while retaining his post as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 賜第一區。

translations.literal: He was granted one premier residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a premier residence.

sentences.zh: 安化軍節度使徒單子溫，平章政事合喜之侄也，贓濫不法，石即劾奏之。

translations.literal: Anhua Army Military Commissioner Tushan Ziwen, nephew of Associate Grand Councillor Hexi, was corrupt and lawless; Shi immediately impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Ziwen, military commissioner of the Anhua Army and nephew of Associate Grand Councillor Hexi, was corrupt and lawless; Shi immediately impeached him.

sentences.zh: 方石奏事，宰相下殿立，俟良久。

translations.literal: While Shi was presenting a memorial, the chief ministers descended from the hall and stood waiting a long time.
translations.idiomatic: While Shi was presenting his memorial, the chief ministers left the hall and stood waiting for a long while.

sentences.zh: 既退，宰相或問石奏事何久，石正色曰：「正為天下姦污未盡誅耳。」

translations.literal: After he withdrew, a chief minister asked why Shi's memorial had taken so long; Shi said sternly: It is because the wicked and corrupt of the realm have not all been put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After he withdrew, a chief minister asked why his memorial had taken so long; Shi said sternly, "Because the wicked and corrupt of the realm have not all been put to death."

sentences.zh: 聞者悚然。

translations.literal: Those who heard were startled.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were startled.

sentences.zh: 一日，上謂石曰：「禦史分別庶官邪、正。

translations.literal: One day the emperor told Shi: The censorate distinguishes the upright and corrupt among common officials.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told Shi: "The censorate distinguishes the upright from the corrupt among officials.

sentences.zh: 卿等惟劾有罪，而未嘗舉善也，宜令監察分路刺舉善惡以聞。」

translations.literal: You only impeach the guilty and never recommend the good; you should have the investigators tour the circuits to report good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: You only impeach the guilty and never recommend the worthy; you should have the investigators tour the circuits and report both good and evil conduct.

sentences.zh: 石司憲既久，年浸高。

translations.literal: Shi had long overseen the law; his years gradually advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had long held charge of the law, and his years were advancing.

sentences.zh: 禦史台奏，事有在制前斷定，乞依新條改斷者。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized that there were cases decided before a new statute who asked to be retried under the new articles.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate memorialized that some cases decided under the previous statute requested retrial under the new articles.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「若在制前行者，豈可改也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: If they were carried out under the previous statute, how can they be changed?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If they were carried out under the previous statute, how can they be changed?"

sentences.zh: 上禦香閣，召中丞移剌道謂之曰：「李石耄矣，汝等宜盡心。

translations.literal: The emperor held court in the Fragrant Pavilion and summoned Vice Censor-in-Chief Yila Dao, telling him: Li Shi is aged; you should all devote yourselves wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court in the Fragrant Pavilion and summoned Vice Censor-in-Chief Yila Dao, telling him: "Li Shi is old; you should all devote yourselves wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 向所奏事甚不當，豈涉於私乎？」

translations.literal: The matters you have reported lately were quite improper—did they involve private interest?
translations.idiomatic: The matters reported lately were quite improper—did they involve private interest?"

sentences.zh: 他日，又謂石曰：「卿近累奏皆常事，臣下善惡邪正，無語及之。

translations.literal: Another day he again told Shi: Your recent repeated memorials are all routine matters; you never speak of good or evil, upright or corrupt among subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he again told Shi: "Your recent memorials are all routine matters; you never speak of good or evil, upright or corrupt conduct among your subordinates.

sentences.zh: 卿年老矣，不能久居此，若能舉一二善事，亦不負此職也。」

translations.literal: You are old and cannot long remain in this post; if you can recommend one or two good deeds, you would not fail in this duty.
translations.idiomatic: You are old and cannot long remain in this post; if you can recommend one or two worthy deeds, you will not have failed in your duty."

sentences.zh: 十年，進拜太尉、尚書令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was advanced to Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was advanced to Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太后兄弟惟卿一人，故命領尚書事。

translations.literal: An edict said: Of the empress dowager's brothers you alone remain; therefore you are ordered to head the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Of the empress dowager's brothers you alone remain; therefore you are ordered to head the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 軍國大事，涉於利害，識其可否，細事不煩卿也。」

translations.literal: In military and state affairs that touch benefit and harm, discern what is feasible; trivial matters will not trouble you.
translations.idiomatic: In military and state affairs that touch on benefit and harm, discern what is feasible; trivial matters will not trouble you."

sentences.zh: 進封平原郡王。

translations.literal: He was further enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was further enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 平章政事完顏守道奏事，石神色不懌。

translations.literal: Associate Grand Councillor Wanyan Shoudao was presenting a memorial; Shi's expression was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Associate Grand Councillor Wanyan Shoudao was presenting a memorial, Shi's expression was displeased.

sentences.zh: 世宗察之，謂石曰：「守道所奏，既非私事，卿當共議可否。

translations.literal: Shizong perceived it and told Shi: What Shoudao memorialized was not a private matter; you should jointly deliberate what is feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong noticed this and told Shi: "What Shoudao memorialized was not a private matter; you should deliberate together whether it is feasible.

sentences.zh: 在上位者所見有不可，順而從之，在下位者所見雖當，則遽不從乎？

translations.literal: If one in a superior position sees something unacceptable yet follows along, and one in an inferior position sees what is right yet abruptly refuses to follow—is that so?
translations.idiomatic: If one in a superior position sees something unacceptable yet goes along with it, while one in an inferior position sees what is right yet abruptly refuses to follow—is that how it should be?

sentences.zh: 豈可以與己相違而蓄怒哉。

translations.literal: How can one harbor anger because it differs from one's own view?
translations.idiomatic: How can one harbor anger simply because it differs from one's own view?

sentences.zh: 如此則下位者誰敢複言？」

translations.literal: If it is like this, who among those below would dare speak again?
translations.idiomatic: If it is like this, who among those below would dare speak up again?"

sentences.zh: 石對曰：「不敢。」

translations.literal: Shi replied: I dare not.
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied: "I dare not."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕欲於京府節鎮運司長佐三員內任文臣一員，尚未得人。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: I wish to appoint one civil official among the three chief associates of the capital prefecture, military commissioners, and transport commission; I have not yet obtained a man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I wish to appoint one civil official among the three chief associates of the capital prefecture, military commissioners, and transport commission, but I have not yet found a suitable man."

sentences.zh: 石奏曰：「資考未至，不敢擬。」

translations.literal: Shi memorialized: Their qualifications and examinations have not yet been met; I dare not nominate.
translations.idiomatic: Shi memorialized: "Their qualifications and examinations have not yet been met; I dare not nominate anyone."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「近觀節度轉運副使中才能者有之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: Of late I have observed that among deputy military commissioners and deputy transport commissioners there are some with ability.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Of late I have observed that among deputy military commissioners and deputy transport commissioners there are men of ability.

sentences.zh: 海陵時，省令史不用進士，故少尹節度轉運副使中乏人。

translations.literal: In Hailing's time the Secretariat clerks did not use jinshi graduates, so among vice magistrates, deputy military commissioners, and deputy transport commissioners men were scarce.
translations.idiomatic: In Hailing's time the Secretariat did not employ jinshi graduates as clerks, so vice magistrates, deputy military commissioners, and deputy transport commissioners were in short supply.

sentences.zh: 大定以來，用進士，亦頗有人矣，節度轉運副使中有廉能者具以名聞，朕將用之。

translations.literal: Since Dading, jinshi have been used and there have been quite a few; among deputy military commissioners and deputy transport commissioners, report by name any who are upright and capable—I will employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Dading, jinshi have been employed and there have been quite a few capable men; report by name any deputy military commissioners or deputy transport commissioners who are upright and able—I will employ them.

sentences.zh: 朝官不曆外任，無以見其才，外官不曆隨朝，無以進其才，中外更試，庶可得人。」

translations.literal: If court officials do not serve outside, there is no way to see their talent; if outside officials do not attend court, there is no way to advance their talent—alternating court and outside service might obtain men.
translations.idiomatic: If court officials never serve outside, there is no way to test their talent; if outside officials never attend court, there is no way to advance their careers—alternating court and outside service may yield the right men."

sentences.zh: 他日，上複問曰：「外任五品職事多闕，何也？」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor again asked: Why are so many fifth-rank outside posts vacant?
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor again asked: "Why are so many fifth-rank outside posts vacant?"

sentences.zh: 石對曰：「資考少有及者。」

translations.literal: Shi replied: Few meet the qualifications and examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied: "Few meet the qualifications and examinations."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「苟有賢能，當不次用之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: If there is worth and ability, they should be employed out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If there is talent and ability, they should be employed out of turn."

sentences.zh: 對不稱旨，上表乞骸骨，乙太保致仕，進封廣平郡王。

translations.literal: His answers did not accord with the imperial intent; he submitted a memorial begging to retire; on the yi day he was made Grand Guardian and retired, and was advanced to Prince of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His answers did not satisfy the emperor; he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; on the yi day he was made Grand Guardian and retired, and was advanced to Prince of Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十六年，薨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 上輟朝臨吊，哭之慟，賻錢萬貫，官給葬事。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court to mourn in person, wept bitterly, granted ten thousand strings of cash as funeral gift, and had the government perform the burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court to mourn him in person, wept bitterly, granted ten thousand strings of cash as a funeral gift, and had the government perform the burial rites.

sentences.zh: 少府監張僅言監護，親王、宰相以下郊送，諡襄簡。

translations.literal: Junior Household Steward Zhang Jinyan supervised the rites; princes, chief ministers, and those below escorted him to the suburbs; posthumous title Xiangjian.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Household Steward Zhang Jinyan supervised the funeral; princes, chief ministers, and officials below escorted the procession to the suburbs; his posthumous title was Xiangjian.

sentences.zh: 石以勳戚，久處腹心之寄，內廷獻替，外罕得聞。

translations.literal: Shi was by imperial grace a long-held confidant at the heart; inner-court counsel and substitutions—outsiders seldom heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: As a meritorious kinsman, Shi had long held the emperor's innermost confidence; his counsel within the palace was seldom known outside.

sentences.zh: 觀其劾奏徒單子溫退答宰臣之問，氣岸宜有不能堪者。

translations.literal: Judging from his impeachment of Tushan Ziwen and his reply when the chief ministers withdrew, his air of authority suggests there were things others could not bear.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from his impeachment of Tushan Ziwen and his reply to the chief ministers' question upon withdrawing, his imposing manner must have been hard for some to bear.

sentences.zh: 時論得失半之，亦豈以是耶？

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion was half right and half wrong—could it be because of that?
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion was divided on his merits and faults—was it perhaps because of this?

sentences.zh: 舊史載其少貧，貞懿後周之，不受，曰：「國家方急用人，正宜自勉，何患乎貧。」

translations.literal: Old histories say that in his youth he was poor and Empress Zhenyì would assist him but he would not accept, saying: The state urgently needs men; one should encourage oneself—what worry is there in poverty?
translations.idiomatic: Older histories record that in his youth he was poor and Empress Zhenyì would help him, but he refused, saying: "The state urgently needs capable men; one should strive to improve oneself—what is there to fear in poverty?"

sentences.zh: 後感泣曰：「汝苟能此，吾複何憂。」

translations.literal: Later she wept and said: If you can be like this, what more have I to fear?
translations.idiomatic: Later she wept and said: "If you can be like this, what more have I to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 及中年，以冒粟見斥，眾譏貪鄙，如出二人。

translations.literal: In mid-life, for seizing grain he was dismissed; the crowd ridiculed him as greedy and base—a different man, as it were.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in mid-life, for seizing grain he was dismissed; the public mocked him as greedy and base—as if he were a different man altogether.

sentences.zh: 史又稱其未貴，人有慢之者，及為相，其人以事見石，惶恐。

translations.literal: The histories also say that before he was eminent, someone treated him lightly; when he became chief minister that person came to see Shi on business in fear and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: The histories also say that before he rose to prominence, someone had treated him with disrespect; when he became chief minister, that person came to see him on business in fear and trembling.

sentences.zh: 石曰：「吾豈念舊惡者。」

translations.literal: Shi said: Am I one who bears old grudges?
translations.idiomatic: Shi said: "Am I one who bears old grudges?"

sentences.zh: 待之彌厚。

translations.literal: He treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: He treated him all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 能為長者言如是，又與他日氣岸迥殊。

translations.literal: To speak as an elder in this way, yet on another day show such a different air of authority!
translations.idiomatic: To speak as a magnanimous elder in this way, yet on another day display such an imposing manner—the contrast is striking.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南軍民交惡，爭田不絕。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians in Shandong and Henan were mutually hostile, incessantly disputing fields.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians in Shandong and Henan were mutually hostile, and disputes over fields never ceased.

sentences.zh: 有司謂兵為國根本，姑宜假借。

translations.literal: The authorities said the army was the state's foundation and fields should for the time being be yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities argued that the army was the foundation of the state and that fields should for the time being be yielded to the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 石持不可，曰：「兵民一也，孰輕孰重？

translations.literal: Shi held that this could not be done, saying: Soldiers and civilians are one—who is light, who heavy?
translations.idiomatic: Shi held that this would not do, saying: "Soldiers and civilians are one and the same—who is lighter, who heavier?

sentences.zh: 國家所恃以立者，紀綱耳，紀綱不明，故下敢輕冒。

translations.literal: What the state relies on to stand is discipline alone; when discipline is unclear, those below dare lightly transgress.
translations.idiomatic: What the state relies upon to endure is discipline alone; when discipline is unclear, those below dare to transgress lightly.

sentences.zh: 惟當明其疆理，示以法禁，使之無爭，是為長久之術。」

translations.literal: Only clarify their boundaries, show the law's prohibitions, and make them cease disputing—this is the long-term method.
translations.idiomatic: One should only clarify their boundaries, display the prohibitions of the law, and make them cease disputing—this is the lasting remedy."

sentences.zh: 趣有司按問，自是軍民之爭遂息。

translations.literal: He urged the authorities to investigate; from then on disputes between soldiers and civilians ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the authorities to investigate; from then on disputes between soldiers and civilians ceased.

sentences.zh: 北京民曹貴謀反，大理議廷中，謂貴等陰謀久不能發，在法「詞理不能動眾，威力不足率人」，罪止論斬。

translations.literal: A civilian of Beijing, Cao Gui, plotted rebellion; the Court of Judicial Review deliberated in court, saying Gui and others had long harbored the plot yet could not launch it; under the law words and reasoning cannot move the multitude and authority and might are insufficient to lead men—the crime was punishable only by execution.
translations.idiomatic: A civilian of Beijing named Cao Gui plotted rebellion; the Court of Judicial Review deliberated in open court, holding that Gui and his accomplices had long harbored the plot but could not carry it out; under the statute that "words and reasoning cannot move the multitude, and authority and might are insufficient to lead men," the offense warranted execution alone.

sentences.zh: 石是之。

translations.literal: Shi approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shi approved this ruling.

sentences.zh: 又議從坐，久不能決。

translations.literal: Deliberation over those implicated lingered long without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation over those implicated by association dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 石曰：「罪疑惟輕。」

translations.literal: Shi said: In doubt of guilt, show leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said: "When guilt is in doubt, show leniency."

sentences.zh: 入，詳奏其狀，上從之，緣坐皆免死。

translations.literal: He entered and reported the facts in detail; the emperor assented, and those implicated were all spared death.
translations.idiomatic: He entered and reported the facts in detail; the emperor assented, and all those implicated by association were spared death.

sentences.zh: 北鄙歲警，朝廷欲發民穿深塹以禦之。

translations.literal: The northern border had annual alarms; the court wished to conscript the people to dig deep moats for defense.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was alarmed year after year; the court wished to conscript the people to dig deep moats for defense.

sentences.zh: 石與丞相紇石烈良弼皆曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Shi and Grand Councillor Hesala Liangbi both said: It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Grand Councillor Hesala Liangbi both said: "It cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 古築長城備北，徒耗民力，無益於事。

translations.literal: In antiquity they built the Long Wall to guard the north, only exhausting the people's strength with no benefit to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity they built the Long Wall to guard the north, only exhausting the people's strength without benefiting the state.

sentences.zh: 北俗無定居，出沒不常，惟當以德柔之。

translations.literal: Northern custom has no fixed abodes; they come and go without pattern—only by virtue should they be softened.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners have no fixed settlements and come and go unpredictably; they can only be appeased through virtue.

sentences.zh: 若徒深塹，必當置戍，而塞北多風沙，曾未期年，塹已平矣。

translations.literal: If one merely digs deep moats, garrisons must be posted; the northern frontier has much wind and sand, and before a year has passed the moats are already level again.
translations.idiomatic: If one merely digs deep moats, garrisons must be stationed; the northern frontier is swept by wind and sand, and before a year has passed the moats are leveled again.

sentences.zh: 不可疲中國有用之力，為此無益。」

translations.literal: One cannot exhaust the useful strength of China for such unprofitable work.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot exhaust the useful strength of the Central Plains on such unprofitable labor."

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 是皆足稱雲。

translations.literal: These are all sufficient to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: These deeds are all worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 世宗在位幾三十年，尚書令凡四人：張浩以舊官，完顏守道以功，徒單克甯以顧命，石以定策，他無及者。

translations.literal: Shizong reigned nearly thirty years; Directors of the Imperial Secretariat numbered four in all: Zhang Hao for old office, Wanyan Shoudao for merit, Tushan Kening for testamentary charge, Shi for settling the succession—no others matched them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong reigned for nearly thirty years; only four men held the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat: Zhang Hao for his long service, Wanyan Shoudao for merit, Tushan Kening as a testamentary minister, and Shi for securing the succession—none others equaled them.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，配享世宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was granted co-worship in Shizong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was granted a place in co-worship at Shizong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 子獻可、逵可。

translations.literal: His sons were Xiankhe and Kuaike.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xiankhe and Kuaike.

sentences.zh: 子 獻可

translations.literal: Son: Xiankhe
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiankhe

sentences.zh: 完顏福壽

translations.literal: Wanyan Fushou
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Fushou

sentences.zh: 完顏福壽，曷速館人也。

translations.literal: Wanyan Fushou was a man of the Yisuoguan.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Fushou was from the Yisuoguan tribe.

sentences.zh: 父合住，國初來歸，授猛安。

translations.literal: His father Hezhu came over at the founding of the state and was granted a meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hezhu submitted at the founding of the dynasty and was granted a meng'an.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，福壽襲父合住職，授定遠大將軍，累加金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan, Fushou inherited his father Hezhu's post, was appointed General Who Fixes the Distance, and rose to Senior General of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan, Fushou inherited his father's position, was appointed General Who Fixes the Distance, and eventually rose to Senior General of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 海陵省並猛安謀克，遂停封。

translations.literal: Hailing consolidated meng'an and mouke, and enfeoffment was then suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing consolidated the meng'an and mouke, hereditary enfeoffment was suspended.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，海陵伐宋，福壽領婁室、台答藹二猛安由山東道進至泰安。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong, when Hailing attacked Song, Fushou led the two meng'an of Loushi and Taidai'ai along the Shandong route to Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenglong era, when Hailing attacked the Song, Fushou led the Loushi and Taidai'ai meng'an along the Shandong route as far as Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 既受甲，福壽乃誘將校北還，而高忠建、盧萬家奴等亦各率眾萬余俱歸東京，欲共立世宗。

translations.literal: After receiving armor, Fushou induced the officers to return north; Gao Zhongjian, Lu Wanjianu, and others each led more than ten thousand men back to Dongjing, wishing jointly to establish Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving their armor, Fushou persuaded the officers to march north; Gao Zhongjian, Lu Wanjianu, and others each led more than ten thousand men back to Dongjing, intending together to install Shizong as emperor.

sentences.zh: 至遼口，世宗遣徒單思忠、府吏張謀魯瓦等來迎，察其去就。

translations.literal: At Liaokou, Shizong sent Tushan Sizhong, prefectural clerk Zhang Moluwa, and others to welcome them and observe their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaokou, Shizong sent Tushan Sizhong, the prefectural clerk Zhang Moluwa, and others to welcome them and discern their intentions.

sentences.zh: 思忠等以數騎馳入軍中，見福壽等問曰：「將軍何為至此？」

translations.literal: Sizhong and others galloped into the army with several horsemen, saw Fushou and the rest, and asked: General, why have you come here?
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong and his companions galloped into the camp with a few horsemen, saw Fushou and the others, and asked: "General, why have you come here?"

sentences.zh: 福壽等向南指海陵而言曰：「此人失道，不能保天下。

translations.literal: Fushou and the rest pointed south toward Hailing and said: This man has lost the Way and cannot preserve the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Fushou and the others pointed south toward Hailing and said: "That man has lost the Way and cannot preserve the realm.

sentences.zh: 國公乃太祖皇帝親孫，我輩欲推戴為主，以此來耳。」

translations.literal: Prince Guo is the founding emperor's own grandson; we wish to install him as sovereign—that is why we have come.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guo is a grandson of the founding emperor; we wish to install him as sovereign—that is why we have come."

sentences.zh: 諸軍皆東向拜，呼萬歲。

translations.literal: All the armies bowed eastward and shouted Ten Thousand Years.
translations.idiomatic: All the troops bowed toward the east and shouted "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 為書以授思忠。

translations.literal: They wrote a letter and gave it to Sizhong.
translations.idiomatic: They wrote a letter and handed it to Sizhong.

sentences.zh: 於是督諸軍渡遼水，徑至東京城下，即諭軍士擐甲入衛宮城，殺高存福等。

translations.literal: Thereupon he urged the armies across the Liao River, went straight to below Dongjing city, immediately ordered the soldiers to don armor and enter to guard the palace city, and killed Gao Cunfu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he urged the armies across the Liao River, marched straight to Dongjing, ordered the soldiers to don armor and enter to guard the palace city, and killed Gao Cunfu and his associates.

sentences.zh: 明日，與諸將及東京吏民從婆速路兵馬都總管完顏謀衍勸進。

translations.literal: The next day, together with the generals and the officials and people of Dongjing, they followed Basulu Army and Horse Metropolitan Commander Wanyan Mouyan in urging enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, together with the generals and the officials and people of Dongjing, they joined Basulu Army and Horse Metropolitan Commander Wanyan Mouyan in urging Shizong to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以福壽為元帥右監軍，賜以銀幣禦馬。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he made Fushou Right Army Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief and granted him silver, coin, and an imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, he appointed Fushou Right Army Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief and granted him silver, coin, and an imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 初，謀衍之至也，大會諸軍，以福壽之軍居左，高忠建軍居右。

translations.literal: At first, when Mouyan arrived, he held a great assembly of the armies, placing Fushou's army on the left and Gao Zhongjian's army on the right.
translations.idiomatic: When Mouyan first arrived, he convened a great assembly of the armies, placing Fushou's force on the left and Gao Zhongjian's on the right.

sentences.zh: 忠建曰：「何以我軍為右軍？」

translations.literal: Zhongjian said: Why is my army made the right army?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjian said: "Why is my army placed on the right?"

sentences.zh: 謀衍曰：「樹置在我，爾曷敢言！」

translations.literal: Mouyan said: The arrangement of ranks is mine—how dare you speak!
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan said: "The arrangement is mine to make—how dare you object!"

sentences.zh: 福壽曰：「始建大事，左右軍高下何足爭也。」

translations.literal: Fushou said: We are just beginning a great enterprise—what is there to dispute over which army is left or right, higher or lower?
translations.idiomatic: Fushou said: "We are only beginning a great enterprise—what is there to dispute over left and right precedence?"

sentences.zh: 遂讓忠建為左軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon yielded to Zhongjian the left army.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon yielded the left position to Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞而賢之。

translations.literal: Shizong heard of it and considered him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong heard of this, he regarded Fushou as admirable.

sentences.zh: 未幾，從完顏謀衍討白彥敬、紇石烈志甯於北京。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Wanyan Mouyan to campaign against Bai Yanjing and Hesala Zhining at Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he followed Wanyan Mouyan to campaign against Bai Yanjing and Hesala Zhining in the north.

sentences.zh: 是冬，上聞臨潢尹兼元帥左都監吾紮忽等與窩斡戰不利，命福壽將兵進討。

translations.literal: That winter, when the emperor heard that the Prefect of Linhuang and concurrently Left Army Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief Wuzhahu and others were faring poorly against Wohe, he ordered Fushou to lead troops forward to attack.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, hearing that the Prefect of Linhuang and concurrently Left Army Supervisor Wuzhahu was faring poorly against Wohe, the emperor ordered Fushou to lead troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 已敗賊，俘獲生口萬計。

translations.literal: He had already defeated the rebels and captured captives numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels and captured captives numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 世宗以紇石烈志寧代之，召還，授興平軍節度使，複其世襲猛安，尋領濟州路諸軍事。

translations.literal: Shizong replaced him with Hesala Zhining and recalled him, appointing him military commissioner of the Xingping Army, restoring his hereditary meng'an, and soon putting him in charge of all military affairs of Jizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong replaced him with Hesala Zhining and recalled him, appointing him military commissioner of the Xingping Army, restoring his hereditary meng'an, and soon placing him in charge of all military affairs in Jizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 獨吉義

translations.literal: Du Jiyi
translations.idiomatic: Du Jiyi

sentences.zh: 獨吉義，本名鶻魯補，曷速館人也。

translations.literal: Du Jiyi, original name Helubu, was a man of the Yisuoguan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jiyi, whose original name was Helubu, was from the Yisuoguan tribe.

sentences.zh: 徙居遼陽之阿米吉山。

translations.literal: His family moved to Amiji Mountain in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family moved to Amiji Mountain in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 祖回海，父秘剌。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Huihai; his father was Mila.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Huihai and his father Mila.

sentences.zh: 改國二年，曷速館來附，秘剌領戶三百，遂為謀克。

translations.literal: In the second year of Gaiguo, when the Yisuoguan submitted, Mila led three hundred households and thus became a mouke.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Gaiguo, when the Yisuoguan submitted, Mila led three hundred households and became a mouke.

sentences.zh: 秘剌長子照屋，次子忽史與義同母。

translations.literal: Mila's eldest son was Zhaowu; his second son Hushi was Yi's uterine brother.
translations.idiomatic: Mila's eldest son was Zhaowu; his second son Hushi was Yi's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 秘剌死，忽史欲承謀克。

translations.literal: When Mila died, Hushi wished to inherit the mouke.
translations.idiomatic: When Mila died, Hushi wished to inherit the mouke.

sentences.zh: 義曰：「長兄雖異母，不可奪也。」

translations.literal: Yi said: The elder brother, though of a different mother, cannot be displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "The elder brother, though born of a different mother, cannot be displaced."

sentences.zh: 忽史乃以謀克歸照屋，人鹹義之。

translations.literal: Hushi thereupon returned the mouke to Zhaowu; all praised Yi's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Hushi thereupon yielded the mouke to Zhaowu, and all praised Yi's righteousness.

sentences.zh: 義以質子至上京。

translations.literal: Yi went to the Upper Capital as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Yi went to the Upper Capital as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 善女直、契丹字，為管勾御前文字。

translations.literal: He was skilled in Jurchen and Khitan script and served as overseer of documents before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in Jurchen and Khitan script, he served as overseer of documents before the throne.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，擢右監門衛大將軍，除甯化州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was promoted to Senior General of the Right Gate Guard and made inspector of Ninghua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was promoted to Senior General of the Right Gate Guard and appointed inspector of Ninghua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 察廉，遷迭剌部族節度使、複州防禦使，改卓魯部族節度使、河南路統軍都監，為武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: Found upright in inspection, he was transferred to military commissioner of the Diela tribal band, defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture, then military commissioner of the Zhuolu tribal band and metropolitan supervisor of the Henan Circuit army, and made military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Found upright in an integrity inspection, he was transferred to military commissioner of the Diela tribal band and defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture, then to military commissioner of the Zhuolu tribal band and metropolitan supervisor of the Henan Circuit army, and finally made military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 邊郡妄稱寇至，統軍司徙居民于汴，義獨不聽，日與官屬擊球遊宴。

translations.literal: Border prefectures falsely reported that bandits had arrived; the army command relocated the populace to Bian, but Yi alone would not obey and daily played ball and feasted with his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Border prefectures falsely reported enemy raids; the army command relocated the populace to Bian, but Yi alone refused and spent his days playing ball and feasting with his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 統軍司使人責之，義曰：「太師梁王南伐淮南，死者未葬，亡者未複，彼豈敢先發？

translations.literal: The army command sent someone to rebuke him; Yi said: Grand Master Prince of Liang is campaigning south against Huainan; the dead are not yet buried, the displaced not yet restored—how would they dare strike first?
translations.idiomatic: The army command sent someone to rebuke him; Yi said: "Grand Master Prince of Liang is campaigning south against Huainan; the dead are not yet buried and the displaced not yet restored—how would they dare strike first?

sentences.zh: 此城中有榷場，若自動，彼將謂我無人。」

translations.literal: This city has a trade mart; if we move on our own, they will think we have no men.
translations.idiomatic: This city has a trade mart; if we stir on our own, they will think we have no one to defend it."

sentences.zh: 既而果無事，統軍謝之，請以沿邊唐州等處諸軍猛安皆隸於義。

translations.literal: Before long there was indeed no trouble; the army command apologized to him and requested that all army meng'an along the border at Tang Prefecture and elsewhere be placed under Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long there was indeed no trouble; the army command apologized and requested that all border army meng'an from Tang Prefecture and elsewhere be placed under Yi's command.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，改唐古部族節度使，為彰化軍，改利涉軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was changed from military commissioner of the Tanggu tribal band to the Zhanghua Army and made military commissioner of the Lishe Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was transferred from military commissioner of the Tanggu tribal band to the Zhanghua Army and appointed military commissioner of the Lishe Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，海陵伐宋，諸軍往往逃歸，而世宗在東京得眾心。

translations.literal: At that time Hailing was attacking Song and armies often fled back; meanwhile Shizong at Dongjing won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hailing was attacking the Song and armies were deserting in droves, while Shizong at Dongjing was winning the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 都統白彥敬自北京使人陰結義，欲與共圖世宗。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Bai Yanjing sent men from Beijing to secretly contact Yi, wishing jointly to plot against Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Bai Yanjing sent envoys from Beijing to secretly contact Yi, intending to plot against Shizong together.

sentences.zh: 頃之，世宗即位，義即日來歸，具陳所以與彥敬密謀者。

translations.literal: Before long Shizong took the throne; Yi came to submit the same day and fully reported his secret plotting with Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shizong took the throne; Yi came to submit the same day and fully disclosed his secret plotting with Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉其不欺，以為參知政事。

translations.literal: Shizong praised his honesty and made him Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong praised his honesty and appointed him Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 子和尚，大定初，除應奉翰林文字，佩金牌。

translations.literal: His son Heshang, at the beginning of Dading, was made Attendant of the Hanlin Academy for Documents and wore a gold tablet.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heshang, at the beginning of Dading, was appointed Attendant of the Hanlin Academy for Documents and wore a gold tablet.

sentences.zh: 陀滿訛裏也子撒曷輦充護衛，司吏王得兒加保義校尉，皆佩銀牌。

translations.literal: Tuoman Eliye's son Sahenian served as guard; clerk Wang De'er was made Defender of Righteousness Commandant—all wore silver tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoman Eliye's son Sahenian served as guard; clerk Wang De'er was made Defender of Righteousness Commandant—all wore silver tablets.

sentences.zh: 持詔書宣諭中都以南州郡，及往南京諭太傅張浩。

translations.literal: Bearing an edict, he announced it to the prefectures and commanderies south of the Central Capital, and went to Nanjing to instruct Grand Tutor Zhang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing an imperial edict, he proclaimed it to the prefectures and commanderies south of the Central Capital, and went to Nanjing to instruct Grand Tutor Zhang Hao.

sentences.zh: 中道聞海陵遇害，南京及都督府皆奉表賀，乃止。

translations.literal: Midway he heard that Hailing had been killed; Nanjing and the metropolitan office all submitted congratulatory memorials, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Midway he learned that Hailing had been assassinated; Nanjing and the metropolitan office had all submitted congratulatory memorials, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 和尚為奉使，擅廢置州縣官，輒行殺戮，詔尚書省鞫治之。

translations.literal: Heshang, as an envoy, on his own authority dismissed and appointed prefectural and county officials and carried out executions; an edict ordered the Imperial Secretariat to investigate and punish him.
translations.idiomatic: As an envoy, Heshang on his own authority dismissed and appointed local officials and carried out executions; an edict ordered the Imperial Secretariat to investigate and punish him.

sentences.zh: 十九年，詔以義孫引壽為斜魯答阿世襲謀克。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, an edict made Yi's grandson Yinshou hereditary mouke of Xieluda'a.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, an edict made Yi's grandson Yinshou hereditary mouke of Xieluda'a.

sentences.zh: 義性辯給，善談論，服玩不尚奢侈，食不兼味雲。

translations.literal: Yi was quick-witted and eloquent, skilled in discussion; his dress and ornaments did not favor luxury, and his food had no more than one flavor at a time.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was quick-witted and eloquent, skilled in debate; he did not favor luxury in dress or ornaments, and never ate more than one dish at a meal.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：章宗嘗問群臣：「世宗初起東京，大臣為誰？」

translations.literal: The encomium says: Zhangzong once asked the ministers: When Shizong first rose at Dongjing, who were his chief ministers?
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Zhangzong once asked his ministers: "When Shizong first rose at Dongjing, who were his chief ministers?"

sentences.zh: 完顏守貞對曰：「止有李石一人。」

translations.literal: Wanyan Shouzhen replied: There was only Li Shi alone.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Shouzhen replied: "There was only Li Shi."

sentences.zh: 章宗歎曰：「苟如此，信有天命也。」

translations.literal: Zhangzong sighed: If it was truly so, Heaven's mandate is indeed to be believed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong sighed: "If that was truly so, then Heaven's mandate is real indeed."

sentences.zh: 完顏謀衍部署諸軍，高忠建爭長，完顏福壽讓忠建而己下之，其功多矣。

translations.literal: Wanyan Mouyan deployed the armies; Gao Zhongjian contended for precedence; Wanyan Fushou yielded to Zhongjian and placed himself below—his merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Mouyan deployed the armies; Gao Zhongjian contended for precedence; Wanyan Fushou yielded to Zhongjian and placed himself below—his merit was considerable.

sentences.zh: 當是時，獨吉義最先至，諸將尚未肯附。

translations.literal: At that time Du Jiyi was the first to arrive, yet the generals were still unwilling to submit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Jiyi was the first to arrive, yet the generals were still unwilling to submit.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，果天也，非人力也。

translations.literal: Spoken from this, it was truly Heaven, not human effort.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, it was truly Heaven's doing, not human effort.

sentences.zh: 烏延蒲離黑

translations.literal: Wuyan Pulihei
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Pulihei

sentences.zh: 烏延蒲離黑，速頻路哲特猛安人，改屬合懶路。

translations.literal: Wuyan Pulihei was a man of the Zhete meng'an of the Supin Route and was later reassigned to the Helan Route.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Pulihei was from the Zhete meng'an of the Supin Route and was later reassigned to the Helan Route.

sentences.zh: 祖思列，預平烏春、窩謀罕之亂，及伐遼、宋，皆有功，追授猛安，贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Silie took part in suppressing the rebellions of Wuchun and Womohan and in campaigns against Liao and Song, all with merit; posthumously he was granted a meng'an and given the title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Silie helped suppress the rebellions of Wuchun and Womohan and campaigned against Liao and Song with distinction; posthumously he was granted a meng'an and the title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 父國也，襲猛安。

translations.literal: His father Guoye inherited the meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guoye inherited the meng'an.

sentences.zh: 蒲離黑從太祖伐遼，勇聞軍中。

translations.literal: Pulihei followed the founding emperor in attacking Liao; his bravery was known throughout the army.
translations.idiomatic: Pulihei followed the founding emperor in the campaign against Liao; his bravery was renowned throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，襲猛安，授甯遠大將軍，累官武甯軍節度使，遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan he inherited the meng'an, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, rose to military commissioner of the Wuning Army, and was transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianjuan he inherited the meng'an, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, rose to military commissioner of the Wuning Army, and was transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，行武威軍都總管。

translations.literal: When Hailing attacked Song, he served as metropolitan commander of the Wuwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing attacked the Song, he served as metropolitan commander of the Wuwei Army.

sentences.zh: 軍還，為順義軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he became military commissioner of the Shunyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was made military commissioner of the Shunyi Army.

sentences.zh: 徒單合喜定秦、隴，蒲離黑統完顏習尼列、顏盞門都兵救德順州，改延安、平涼尹。

translations.literal: When Tushan Hexi pacified Qin and Long, Pulihei commanded the troops of Wanyan Xinilie and Yanzhan Mendu to rescue Deshun Prefecture; he was changed to metropolitan magistrate of Yan'an and Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tushan Hexi pacified Qin and Long, Pulihei commanded the forces of Wanyan Xinilie and Yanzhan Mendu to relieve Deshun Prefecture; he was then appointed metropolitan magistrate of Yan'an and Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 致仕，封任國公。

translations.literal: He retired and was enfeoffed as Duke of Renguo.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and was enfeoffed as Duke of Renguo.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the nineteenth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 烏延蒲轄奴

translations.literal: Wuyan Puxianu
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Puxianu

sentences.zh: 烏延蒲轄奴，速頻路星顯河人也，後改隸曷懶路。

translations.literal: Wuyan Puxianu was a man of the Xingxian River in the Supin Route and was later reassigned to the Yilan Route.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Puxianu was from the Xingxian River in the Supin Route and was later reassigned to the Yilan Route.

sentences.zh: 父忽撒渾，天輔初，追授猛安，親管謀克。

translations.literal: His father Husahun, at the beginning of Tianfu, was posthumously granted a meng'an and personally oversaw the mouke.
translations.idiomatic: His father Husahun was posthumously granted a meng'an at the beginning of Tianfu and personally oversaw the mouke.

sentences.zh: 蒲轄奴身長有力，多智略，襲其父猛安謀克，階甯遠大將軍。

translations.literal: Puxianu was tall and strong, full of stratagems; he inherited his father's meng'an and mouke and held the rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Puxianu was tall and powerful and full of stratagems; he inherited his father's meng'an and mouke and held the rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，授陳州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，改昌武軍節度使，以善綏撫，再任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was changed to military commissioner of the Changwu Army; for skill in pacification he was appointed a second term.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to military commissioner of the Changwu Army; for his skill in pacification he was given a second term.

sentences.zh: 海陵南征，改歸德尹，為神策軍都總管。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned south, he was changed to metropolitan magistrate of Guide and made metropolitan commander of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing campaigned south, he was made metropolitan magistrate of Guide and metropolitan commander of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 當屯濟州，比至山東，盜已據其城。

translations.literal: He was to garrison Jizhou; by the time he reached Shandong, bandits had already seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was to garrison Jizhou; by the time he reached Shandong, bandits had already seized the city.

sentences.zh: 蒲轄奴領十餘騎往覘之，忽為其眾所圍。

translations.literal: Puxianu led a dozen horsemen to reconnoiter and was suddenly surrounded by their host.
translations.idiomatic: Puxianu led a dozen horsemen to reconnoiter and was suddenly surrounded by the enemy host.

sentences.zh: 乃與軍士皆下馬，立而射之，殺百餘人。

translations.literal: He and the soldiers all dismounted, stood and shot, and killed more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He and his soldiers all dismounted, stood their ground, and shot, killing more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 賊眾敗走，迤邐襲之，至暮而還。

translations.literal: The rebel host fled in defeat; he pursued them along the way and returned at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled in defeat; he pursued them and returned at dusk.

sentences.zh: 明日，攻破其城，號令士卒，毋害居民，郡中獲安。

translations.literal: The next day he stormed the city, ordered the soldiers not to harm the residents, and the commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he stormed the city, ordered his soldiers not to harm the residents, and the commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 民感其惠，為立祠以祭。

translations.literal: The people were moved by his kindness and erected a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people were moved by his kindness and erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，為慶陽尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he became metropolitan magistrate of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he became metropolitan magistrate of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 元帥左都監徒單合喜奏宋軍十萬餘據險阻，剽掠郡邑，請益師。

translations.literal: Left Army Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief Tushan Hexi memorialized that more than a hundred thousand Song troops held difficult terrain and raided commanderies and districts, requesting reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Left Army Supervisor Tushan Hexi memorialized that more than a hundred thousand Song troops held difficult terrain and were raiding commanderies and districts, requesting reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 詔益兵七千，與舊兵合為二萬。

translations.literal: An edict added seven thousand troops, which with the existing force totaled twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added seven thousand troops, bringing the total force to twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 遣蒲轄奴與延安尹高景山等分領其軍以往。

translations.literal: Puxianu was sent with Yan'an metropolitan magistrate Gao Jingshan and others to divide command of the army and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Puxianu was sent with Yan'an metropolitan magistrate Gao Jingshan and others to divide command of the army and advance.

sentences.zh: 卒於軍，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died in the army at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the field at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子查剌。

translations.literal: His son was Chala.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chala.

sentences.zh: 烏延查剌

translations.literal: Wuyan Chala
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Chala

sentences.zh: 烏延查剌，銀青光祿大夫蒲轄奴子也。

translations.literal: Wuyan Chala was the son of Puxianu, Silver-Green-Blue Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Chala was the son of Puxianu, who held the title Silver-Green-Blue Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 力兼數人，勇果無敵。

translations.literal: His strength matched several men; in courage and daring he was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: He had the strength of several men and was unmatched in courage and daring.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年伐宋，諸猛安謀克兵皆行，州縣無備。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong [the Jin] attacked Song; all meng'an and mouke troops marched out, and the prefectures and counties were undefended.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Song in the sixth year of Zhenglong, every meng'an and mouke unit was deployed, leaving the prefectures and counties without defense.

sentences.zh: 契丹括裏陷韓州，圍信州，遠近震駭。

translations.literal: The Khitan Kuoli took Han Prefecture and besieged Xin Prefecture; near and far were shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan leader Kuoli seized Han Prefecture and besieged Xin Prefecture, spreading terror throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 查剌道出咸平，遂率本部亟還信州，與戰敗之。

translations.literal: Chala was traveling out of Xianping and immediately led his command back to Xin Prefecture in haste; he gave battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Chala happened to be passing through Xianping; he at once led his command back to Xin Prefecture and defeated the enemy in battle.

sentences.zh: 已而賊複整兵環攻，且登其城，查剌下巨木壓之，殺賊甚眾，括裏乃解去。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits regrouped, surrounded and attacked, and even scaled the walls; Chala rolled down huge logs to crush them, killing very many bandits, and Kuoli then broke off and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon regrouped, encircled the city, and began scaling the walls. Chala rolled down massive logs on them, killing a great many, whereupon Kuoli broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 查剌左右手持兩大鐵簡，簡重數十斤，人號為「鐵簡萬戶」。

translations.literal: Chala held a great iron mace in each hand; each mace weighed several tens of jin, and people called him "Iron-Mace Wanhu."
translations.idiomatic: Chala wielded a heavy iron mace in each hand—each weighing dozens of jin—and people called him "Iron-Mace Wanhu."

sentences.zh: 追及括裏于韓州東八里許，賊方就平野為陣，查剌身率銳士，以鐵簡左右揮擊之。

translations.literal: He overtook Kuoli about eight li east of Han Prefecture; the bandits had just drawn up in formation on the open plain, and Chala personally led picked troops, swinging his iron maces left and right to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He caught up with Kuoli some eight li east of Han Prefecture. The rebels had just formed up on the open plain when Chala personally led his elite troops, swinging his iron maces to left and right.

sentences.zh: 無不僵僕。

translations.literal: None failed to fall stiff to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: None who were struck failed to fall dead.

sentences.zh: 賊不能成列，乃易馬督軍複擊之。

translations.literal: The bandits could not hold formation; he changed horses, rallied the army, and attacked again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels could not hold their lines; he remounted, rallied his troops, and attacked again.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大敗，遂走，東京、咸平、隆州民複帖然。

translations.literal: The rebel host suffered a great defeat and fled; the people of Eastern Capital, Xianping, and Long Prefecture were again settled and compliant.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed and fled; the people of Eastern Capital, Xianping, and Long Prefecture were pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 窩斡平，以為宿直將軍，賜銀三百兩、重彩二十端。

translations.literal: When Wohe was pacified, [Chala] was made Palace Guard General and granted three hundred taels of silver and twenty bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: After the suppression of Wohe's rebellion, Chala was appointed Palace Guard General and awarded three hundred taels of silver and twenty bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，以本官起複，襲其父猛安，除蔡州防禦使，改宿州，遷昌武軍節度使，徙鎮邠州。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he was recalled from mourning while retaining his original office, inherited his father's meng'an, was appointed defense commissioner of Cai Prefecture, transferred to Suzhou, promoted to military commissioner of the Changwu Army, and reassigned to govern Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he was recalled from mourning while retaining his rank, inherited his father's meng'an, and was appointed defense commissioner of Cai Prefecture, then transferred to Suzhou, promoted to military commissioner of the Changwu Army, and finally reassigned to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為賀宋歲元使，射淮上柳樹，矢入其樹飲羽。

translations.literal: As envoy to congratulate Song on the New Year, he shot at a willow on the Huai River; the arrow entered the tree up to the feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as envoy to convey New Year's greetings to Song, he shot at a willow on the Huai River—the arrow sank into the trunk up to the fletching.

sentences.zh: 宋人素聞其名，甚異之。

translations.literal: The Song people had long heard his name and were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court had long known his reputation and was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 改鳳翔尹，入為右副點檢，出為興中尹，改婆速路總管。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as metropolitan magistrate of Fengxiang, entered the capital as Right Vice Inspector, went out as metropolitan magistrate of Xingzhong, and was changed to commander-in-chief of the Pasu Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Fengxiang, then recalled to serve as Right Vice Inspector, sent out as metropolitan magistrate of Xingzhong, and finally appointed commander-in-chief of the Pasu Route.

sentences.zh: 高麗憚其威名，凡以事至婆速路者，望見而跪之。

translations.literal: Goryeo feared his formidable name; whenever anyone came to the Pasu Route on business, they knelt at the sight of him.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo feared his reputation; envoys coming to the Pasu Route on business would kneel at the mere sight of him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，為興平軍節度使，卒官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year [of Dading] he was military commissioner of the Xingping Army and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he served as military commissioner of the Xingping Army and died in office.

sentences.zh: 查剌貞愨寡言，平居極和易，及臨戰奮勇，見者無不辟易，雖重圍萬眾，出入若無人之境雲。

translations.literal: Chala was upright, sincere, and sparing of speech; in ordinary life he was exceedingly gentle and easygoing, but when battle came he fought with fierce courage—those who saw him all gave way; though hemmed in by ten thousand men he entered and left as if in an empty land, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Chala was upright and reticent; in peacetime he was genial and easygoing, yet in battle he fought with terrible ferocity—all who faced him shrank back. Even surrounded by tens of thousands, he moved in and out of the fray as though no one were there, it is said.

sentences.zh: 李師雄

translations.literal: Li Shixiong
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixiong

sentences.zh: 李師雄，字伯威，雁門人也。

translations.literal: Li Shixiong, style name Bowei, was a man of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixiong, style name Bowei, was from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 有材力，喜談兵，慕古之英雄，故名師雄。

translations.literal: He had talent and strength, delighted in discoursing on warfare, and admired the heroes of antiquity—hence his style name Shixiong ["Master Hero"].
translations.idiomatic: Talented and strong, he loved to talk of military matters and admired the heroes of old—hence his style name Shixiong, "Master Hero."

sentences.zh: 宋宣和中以騎射登科，累官大名、清平尉。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era of Song he passed the mounted-archery examination and successively served as captain at Daming and Qingping.
translations.idiomatic: During Song's Xuanhe era he qualified through the mounted-archery examination and rose to serve as captain at Daming and Qingping.

sentences.zh: 王師至大名，師雄與府僚出降，攝本路兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When the Jin army reached Daming, Shixiong and the prefectural staff went out to surrender; he was appointed acting military supervisor of the route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army reached Daming, Shixiong and the prefectural staff surrendered; he was appointed acting route military supervisor.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，以為大總管府先鋒都統制，知淄州。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established he was made vanguard commander-in-chief of the Great Commandery Headquarters and prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the puppet Qi state was established, he was appointed vanguard commander-in-chief of the Great Commandery Headquarters and assigned to govern Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊廢，為汴京馬軍都虞候，曆知甯海軍、曹州刺史。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished he became chief adjutant of the Bianjing horse army and successively governed as prefect of Ninghai Army and Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's abolition he became chief adjutant of the Bianjing horse army and later served as prefect of Ninghai Army and Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，為武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he was military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangtong he was appointed military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，為河州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong he was defense commissioner of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenglong era he served as defense commissioner of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋將吳璘軍攻秦、隴，會師雄以事就逮臨洮，宋兵至城下，州人乘城拒守，謀欲出降，師雄止之。

translations.literal: Song general Wu Lin's army attacked Qin and Long; Shixiong happened to have been arrested and taken to Lintao on another matter; Song troops came beneath the walls; the people of the prefecture manned the walls to resist and planned to surrender, but Shixiong stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: When Song general Wu Lin attacked Qin and Long, Shixiong happened to have been taken into custody at Lintao on another matter. Song troops reached the city walls; the townspeople mounted the defenses but planned to surrender—Shixiong persuaded them to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 宋將權儀鞭馬方上浮橋，師雄射之，墜於橋下，遂擒權儀，宋師退。

translations.literal: Song general Quan Yi was whipping his horse just as it mounted the pontoon bridge; Shixiong shot him and he fell beneath the bridge; they then captured Quan Yi and the Song army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: As Song general Quan Yi spurred his horse onto the pontoon bridge, Shixiong shot him; Quan Yi fell beneath the bridge, was captured, and the Song army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後從元帥左監軍徒單合喜以兵攻河州，有功。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Left Army Supervisor of the Commander-in-Chief, Tushan Hexi, in attacking He Prefecture with troops and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Left Army Supervisor Tushan Hexi in the assault on He Prefecture and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾歸汴，卒。

translations.literal: Before long, ill, he returned to Bian and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he returned to Bian due to illness and died.

sentences.zh: 尼厖古鈔兀

translations.literal: Nipangguchaowu
translations.idiomatic: Nipangguchaowu

sentences.zh: 尼厖古鈔兀，曷速館人。

translations.literal: Nipangguchaowu was a man of Yisuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Nipangguchaowu was from Yisuguan.

sentences.zh: 初為大抃紮也，補元帥府通事。

translations.literal: At first he was a daban zhaoye ["great servant youth"] and was appointed interpreter at the Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a household servant and was appointed interpreter at the Marshal's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 宋將韓世忠率軍數萬圍邳州，鈔兀將輕騎數百與偵人數輩間道往救之，敗敵兵六千。

translations.literal: Song general Han Shizhong led an army of tens of thousands to besiege Pi Prefecture; Chaowu led several hundred light cavalry and a few scouts by a side path to rescue it and defeated six thousand enemy troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Song general Han Shizhong besieged Pi Prefecture with tens of thousands of troops, Chaowu led several hundred light cavalry and a handful of scouts by a hidden route to relieve the city, defeating six thousand enemy soldiers.

sentences.zh: 翌日，宋兵複圍下邳，鈔兀複敗之。

translations.literal: The next day Song troops again besieged Xiapi; Chaowu again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Song forces besieged Xiapi again; Chaowu routed them once more.

sentences.zh: 宋人攻濟州，奪戰艦略盡。

translations.literal: The Song attacked Ji Prefecture and seized nearly all the war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Song attacked Ji Prefecture and captured nearly all its war vessels.

sentences.zh: 是時，鈔兀往宿州，分蒲魯虎軍，還至大河，與敵遇，力戰敗之，盡複戰艦。

translations.literal: At that time Chaowu had gone to Suzhou to divide Puluhu's army; returning to the Great River he met the enemy, fought fiercely and defeated them, and fully recovered the war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chaowu had gone to Suzhou to detach part of Puluhu's army. On his return to the Yellow River he encountered the enemy, fought them off, and recovered all the war vessels.

sentences.zh: 王師複河南，宋別將由胡陵夜襲孛堇布輝營，士卒盡沒。

translations.literal: When the imperial army recovered Henan, a separate Song commander raided Commander Buhui's camp by night via Huling; the soldiers were all wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin recovery of Henan, a detached Song force raided Commander Buhui's camp at night through Huling, wiping out his entire force.

sentences.zh: 鈔兀從東平總管並力戰，卻之。

translations.literal: Chaowu joined the Dongping route commander in fighting with combined strength and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Chaowu joined the Dongping route commander in a combined assault and drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 元帥府賞以銀幣。

translations.literal: The Marshal's Headquarters rewarded him with silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Marshal's Headquarters rewarded him with silver and silk currency.

sentences.zh: 鈔兀勇敢，善伺敵虛實，以此屢捷。

translations.literal: Chaowu was brave and skilled at probing the enemy's strengths and weaknesses; by this means he repeatedly won victories.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and skilled at reading the enemy's dispositions, Chaowu won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 帥府承制加忠顯校尉，為蕃部禿裏，賜錢萬貫、幣帛三百匹、衣一襲、馬二匹。

translations.literal: The headquarters, by imperial commission, promoted him to Loyal and Illustrious Captain, made him tuli of the tribal department, and granted ten thousand strings of cash, three hundred bolts of silk currency, one suit of clothing, and two horses.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial commission the headquarters promoted him to Loyal and Illustrious Captain, appointed him tribal tuli, and granted ten thousand strings of cash, three hundred bolts of silk, a suit of clothing, and two horses.

sentences.zh: 將之官，河間尹大抃白于元帥，請留鈔兀以給邊事，許之。

translations.literal: As he was about to take up his post, Metropolitan Magistrate Daban of Hejian reported to the marshal, asking that Chaowu be retained to supply border affairs; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart for his new post, Hejian metropolitan magistrate Daban petitioned the marshal to retain Chaowu for frontier duty; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 複賜錢萬貫、銀二百五十兩、重彩三百端、馬三匹。

translations.literal: He was again granted ten thousand strings of cash, two hundred fifty taels of silver, three hundred bolts of heavy silk, and three horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was further awarded ten thousand strings of cash, two hundred fifty taels of silver, three hundred bolts of fine silk, and three horses.

sentences.zh: 錄功，授慶陽少尹。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was appointed vice metropolitan magistrate of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were entered in the records and he was appointed vice metropolitan magistrate of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 鈔兀與完顏思敬有隙，思敬為北京留守，奉詔至招討司，鈔兀不出餞。

translations.literal: Chaowu and Wanyan Sijing had a grudge; Sijing was Northern Capital Left-Behind Administrator and came by imperial order to the Pacification Commission; Chaowu did not come out to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: Chaowu bore a grudge against Wanyan Sijing. When Sijing, as Northern Capital Left-Behind Administrator, arrived at the Pacification Commission on imperial orders, Chaowu refused to come out to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，遣使切責之曰：「卿本大抃紮也，起身細微。

translations.literal: Shizong heard of this and sent an envoy to rebuke him sharply, saying: "You were originally a daban zhaoye, rising from humble beginnings.
